pharm: Organochlorine pediculicide/scabicide; CNS stimulant toxin to parasites
summary: Lindane is a topical organochlorine pediculicide and scabicide reserved as second-line treatment for head lice, crab (pubic) lice and scabies only in patients who cannot tolerate or have failed safer first-line therapies. It carries a boxed warning: seizures and deaths have occurred, especially with repeat or prolonged application, overdose, or in low-weight patients, the elderly, and those with broken skin. It is applied once as a thin layer and rinsed off; it is never repeated routinely.
indications: Head lice (Pediculus humanus capitis) — second-line, shampoo

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer to dry hair, work in, leave 4 minutes only, then add water, lather briefly and rinse thoroughly; comb out nits
dosage.n: Do not repeat; use minimum amount (max ~30-60 mL per use)

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer to dry skin from the neck down, leave on 8-12 hours, then wash off completely
dosage.n: Do not retreat; use minimum amount (~30-60 mL per use)

admin: Use only as second-line therapy after safer agents fail or are not tolerated
Apply to dry, cool skin/hair; never after a hot bath
Use the smallest amount that covers the area and observe contact-time limits strictly
Do not apply to open wounds, raw or inflamed skin, or mucous membranes
Never re-treat for persistent itching; itching can persist after successful treatment
moa: Organochlorine that is absorbed through the parasite cuticle and acts as a central nervous system stimulant, causing convulsions and death of lice and mites; the same mechanism produces human neurotoxicity when systemically absorbed.

relative: Conditions that increase seizure risk or with concomitant seizure-threshold-lowering drugs
Low body weight, infants and young children
Broken, inflamed or extensive skin disease

preg: Avoid; potential for systemic absorption and neurotoxicity. Use safer alternatives (e.g., permethrin) during pregnancy.
lact: Excreted in breast milk; avoid, or interrupt breastfeeding and discard milk for at least 24 hours if used.
renal: Use caution; impaired clearance may increase systemic exposure and neurotoxicity.
hepatic: Use caution; reduced metabolism may raise systemic levels and seizure risk.

major: Drugs that lower the seizure threshold (certain antipsychotics, antidepressants, antimalarials, systemic antibiotics) — increased seizure risk; avoid concurrent use
moderate: Oils, creams or occlusive dressings on the same skin — increase systemic absorption
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; may add to CNS effects.

common: Local skin irritation, burning or stinging
serious: Seizures (including in patients with no prior seizure history)
Death (with overdose, repeat/prolonged use, or in susceptible patients)

monitoring: Neurologic symptoms after application (especially in children, elderly, low weight)
Correct application technique and contact time
Skin integrity and extent of dermatitis
counsel: Use only as directed; this is a second-line medicine
Apply a thin layer and rinse/wash off exactly on time — leaving it longer is dangerous, not better
Do not re-apply even if itching continues; itching can persist after cure
Keep away from eyes, mouth and broken skin
Seek emergency care for any seizure or if the product is swallowed
pk: Parasiticidal during the limited contact period
Systemic peak ~6 hours after application (if absorbed)
20-25 C (68-77 F), keep away from children
pearls: Boxed warning: seizures and deaths reported, even after a single correct application in susceptible people
Strictly second-line — use only after permethrin or other safer agents fail or are not tolerated
One application only; never re-treat for residual itch
Highest neurotoxicity risk in infants, low-weight patients, the elderly and those with broken/inflamed skin
Banned for agricultural use and restricted in many countries; California banned pharmaceutical use
missed: A single application is the complete course; there is no repeat dose. Do not re-apply if you think you missed coverage without medical advice.
overdose: Systemic toxicity (CNS stimulation, seizures) may follow overuse, prolonged contact, or ingestion. For ingestion do not induce emesis (aspiration/seizure risk); control seizures with benzodiazepines, provide supportive care and seek emergency/poison-control help. Remove from skin by washing.
